newsitem.title: USA: Magnesium shipments in 1996 second highest - IMA.
newsitem.headline: Magnesium shipments in 1996 second highest - IMA.

text.p: Although primary magnesium shipments last year fell 3 percent or 8,600 tonnes to a total of 295,400 tonnes, they were still the second highest on record, International Magnesium Association said.
But inventories contiue to rise, almost doubling from where they were at the end of 1995.
Last year's shipments included an estimated 66,400 tonnes of exports from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and China.
The CIS and China's share of the world market continued to rise last year, reaching 22 percent, up from 15 percent in 1994 and 18 percent in 1995.
Last year's aluminum alloying shipments of 138,200 tonnes were down 18,900 tonnes, or 12 percent, with significant decreases in North America, Western Europe and Japan.

The use of magnesium in desulphurizing steel rose 3,300 tonnes or 9 percent to 39,600 tonnes. Industry sources estimated an additional 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes of scrap is being supplied to this market, the IMA said.
Shipments of magnesium to the die-casting sector were up 8,200 tonnes or 13 percent to 72,300 tonnes, with North America accounting for most of the increase.
The use of magnesium in auto die-cast components is the light metal's brightest growth prospect.
Western world production was only 100 tonnes higher at 248,300 tonnes last year,
Inventories at the end of 1996 totaled 42,100 tonnes, up 19,300 tonnes from the end of 1995, and up 3,700 tonnes from the end of the third quarter of 1996.
